commits.subject: fix(comms-outbox): a refused-channel row no longer counts as needing the recruiter
chore(perf): comms-dispatch keeps its channel constants local; ceiling back to 230

rule: A row needs a human when its verdict is 'orphaned' (the integrator's to chase) or resendDoorOf gives it a door. isActionable (Comms Center) and isDeadLetter (dev-case outbox) both read that, so a failed row on REFUSED_COMMS_CHANNEL (or the simulation channel) no longer drives the red tint, the needs-you count or the dead-letter chip.
decisions: No new shared predicate was needed: resendDoorOf already is the one rule. The only extra case is 'orphaned', which offers no door but still needs the integrator, so it is kept explicitly in both callers.

isActionable now derives commsVerdict(m) first. Behaviour is the same for every flagged row. The one edge that moves: a raw 'bounced' status row with no orphaned flag already reads 'orphaned' in statusTone, and it now counts too.

OutboxRows still prints failureDetail on every failed row, refused included: '(m.verdict === "failed" || isDeadLetter(m)) && m.failureDetail'. Otherwise the refusal reason would have disappeared with the tint. The source-guard regex in outboxView.test.ts was updated to match.

comms-dispatch.ts declares SIM_COMMS_CHANNEL / REFUSED_COMMS_CHANNEL locally, following the r07 jobs-table-core/A precedent. Existing importers from comms-dispatch are unchanged. comms-dispatch-channels.test.ts pins that the two copies are equal and that the import is gone.
The code change and the budget are in ONE commit under the lock, so the budget in each commit matches the graph it measures.
red_first: channelsCommsHelpers.test.ts 1 of 9 failed; outboxView.test.ts 1 of 12 failed; comms-dispatch-channels.test.ts 1 of 2 failed against HEAD's comms-dispatch.ts (the import guard; the equality case held by construction)
